input:
Our Android device randomly reboots after roughly 30 minutes of 4K video recording. The kernel panic log shows:

  [1823.447] thermal thermal_zone3: Trip point 2 crossed. Throttling CPU cluster to 1209600 kHz
  [1823.451] v4l2-dma-contig: failed to alloc 33554432 bytes DMA buffer
  [1823.452] mtk-isp: pipe_1: DMA buffer starvation, dropping frame 1041
  [1823.453] mtk-isp: too many consecutive frame drops, triggering pipeline reset
  [1823.461] Kernel panic - not syncing: hung_task: blocked for more than 120 seconds

The thermal_zone3 is mapped to the ISP cluster. Our thermal policy sets DRAM frequency floor to 800 MHz but clearly that is not preventing the issue. Is this a thermal throttle causing DMA buffer starvation, or is the DMA allocator itself the culprit? How do I triage the root cause between the thermal subsystem and the ISP DMA pipeline?
